The town lies about 12 km east of the historic city of Sukhothai, the former capital of the first Thai kingdom, usually called the Sukhothai Kingdom.

Sukhothai is `a historic destination in north-central Thailand renowned as the capital of the first independent Thai kingdom in the 13th century` . Key highlights include the [Sukhothai Historical Park](https://www.tourismthailand.org/Destinations/Provinces/Sukhothai/114) , Wat Mahathat, and Wat Si Chum.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukhothai_%28city%29) [[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukhothai_%28city%29)[[2]](https://www.belaroundtheworld.com/things-to-do-in-sukhothai-thailand/)[[3]](https://www.tourismthailand.org/Destinations/Provinces/Sukhothai/114)

History and Layout

- **Old and New Towns:** The area is split into Old Sukhothai (the ancient walled ruins) and New Sukhothai (Sukhothai Thani, the modern commercial hub 12 km east).[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukhothai_Thani) [[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukhothai_Thani)[[2]](https://www.thelongestwayhome.com/travel-guides/thailand/sukhothai/sukhothai-city.html)
- **Cradle of Thai Culture:** Founded in 1238, the name translates to "dawn of happiness". It is where the first Thai alphabet and classic art styles originated.[](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7iviLTpF8TU&vl=en&t=5) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7iviLTpF8TU&vl=en&t=5)[[2]](https://www.bucketlistly.blog/posts/sukhothai-best-things-to-do)
- **UNESCO Status:** Designated a World Heritage Site in 1991 alongside sister historic towns Si Satchanalai and Kamphaeng Phet.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukhothai_%28city%29) 

Key Sites to Visit

- **Wat Mahathat:** The massive spiritual center featuring classic lotus-bud spires and royal assembly halls.
- **Wat Si Chum:** Home to Phra Achana, a towering 15-meter seated Buddha statue enclosed in a tight brick chamber.
- **Ramkhamhaeng National Museum:** Houses ancient stone inscriptions and artifacts excavated from the ruins.[](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7iviLTpF8TU&vl=en&t=5) [[1]](https://www.honeytrek.com/sukhothai-thailand-travel/)

Practical Travel Tips

- **Park Entry:** General admission to the central zone of the Sukhothai Historical Park costs 100 Baht.
- **Getting Around:** Renting a bicycle (20–30 Baht) or a motorbike is the best way to explore the sprawling temple grounds. Local songthaews run regularly between the new and old towns for about 30 Baht.[](https://www.theblondtravels.com/sukhothai-things-to-do) [[1]](https://www.theblondtravels.com/sukhothai-things-to-do)

items.title: Is Sukhothai, Thailand worth visiting?
Why was Sukhothai abandoned?

expanded_element.title: A guide to the ruins of Sukhothai, Thailand | National Geographic
expanded_element.description: The kingdom was conquered and absorbed by the Ayutthaya kingdom in 1438. After losing its place as the seat of power, Sukhothai was abandoned in the late 15th or early 16th century. The wooden houses and even royal palaces of Sukhothai's heyday vanished completely over the years.

items.title: How far is Bangkok from Sukhothai?

expanded_element.title: Distance from Bangkok to Sukhothai (BKK – THS) | Air Miles Calculator
expanded_element.description: The air distance between Bangkok (Suvarnabhumi Airport – BKK) and Sukhothai (Sukhothai Airport – THS) is 252.3 miles (406 kilometers or 219.2 nautical miles). The driving distance from Bangkok to Sukhothai is 285.3 miles (459.1 kilometers), with an estimated driving time of approximately 5 hours and 37 minutes.
